notes.title: v0.2 Hotfix
notes.notes:
1.) v0.2 proved to be pretty incompatible with a couple of mods, specifically ones that added spells or skills to your hotbar that didn't otherwise exist in the game. The result was some failed file loads, and lost skills / items / spells, etc. 

I've added some checks in the game's code to help prevent data loss issues for players, but the mods will likely still not work. 



2.) Previously, SimPlayers needed to zone or leave a group to acquire new spells. This worked fine on Stowaway's Step because by design players were zoning in and out of the tomb. 

Willowwatch offers a different play area, which encourages players to remain in the zone for an extended time meaning SimPlayers were not refreshing their spell lists at all.

SimPlayers now have gotten better at planning, and they've pre-bought their spells so when they level up they'll have them at their disposal immediately. 



3.) Fixed some UI issues as reported. 

Thank you for your patience!
Brian

notes.title: Erenshor V0.2 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43905293/e4374bd15770f78d21ce8bce847ed6850656b3d1.png"]


Hello Adventurers!


Here are the patch notes for Erenshor v0.2, releasing on 9/26!



New Class: A fresh class has been added - The STORMCALLER - complete with new skills and spells.

-Stormcallers are skilled in Archery and Storm magic. They combine magic and arrows to do incredibly bursty DPS, crowd control, and are fantastic solo classes. 

Archery & Bows: You can now equip bows and rain arrows on your enemies.

Alternate Start: Players no longer have to start on Stowaway's Step and can elect to begin their journey directly on Erenshor, without a guided tutorial quest to complete.

Base run speed reduced (11 → 8) to balance overall pacing and weight of movement

Strafing and backward movement speeds lowered to be slower than forward movement.

Party size increased to five (Player + 4 SimPlayers).

Reworked Group Roles window with full healing matrix support for more precise control.

Reworked Group Roles puller settings to allow for more control over SimPlayer autopulling

SimPlayers now choose healing spells more intelligently based on the situation.

Higher-level enemies gain new tricks:

Spectral Strike: Hits a secondary target for reduced damage.

Enrage: Damage increases the longer they fight.

Powerful Strike: A periodic hit 4-6x stronger than normal, preceded by a text warning.

Many enemies gained unique AE or other abilities

Can now inspect SimPlayers from further away for easier gear management and trading.

Added Time Stones – consumable items that allow players to reset dungeon spawns at will.

Added Braxonian Fossils - pricey vendor item in Braxonian Desert that have a chance to contain rare loot.

Arcanists get a new Channeling Skill: end a spell early and still have it cast, or channel it past 100% for bonus damage!

Proficiency and Respec system added, allowing for new areas of character customization

-Character "proficiency scores" determine how well that character uses a skill. e.g. You can be a paladin who focuses on strength for DPS, or a paladin who focuses on Endurance and Agility to be a better tank.

-Players and SimPlayers can respec proficiencies at no cost in Fernalla's Revival Plains. Experiment!

-"Charm" items directly affect proficiency scores.

6+ new quests added.

Charm Slot items now grant proficiencies instead of flat stats.

Monster spawn timers adjusted in several zones.
[hr][/hr]UI
Inventory, Stat Screen, and SimPlayer Stat Screen all reworked.

All in-game fonts reworked for size and more consistency

New visible stats: Haste, Attack Bonus, Mana Regen, Health Regen.

More UI elements are movable.

Target window upgrades: % life remaining, Target-of-Target, and optional level-of-target display (see server admin panel)

"Modern Control" setting now persist between sessions for players who prefer that system.

UI elements lost off-screen automatically reset back on-screen at launch (can be disabled in options)

DPS meter optimized for better performance and more accurate info.

Party window now shows HP and Mana numbers.

Druid pets no longer appear as hostile dots on the minimap.

More Status Effect slots for all targets and players to prevent buffs not taking hold
[hr][/hr]Stat Squish
Full item rebalance: Stats lowered across the board, but relative item power remains.

Full spell rebalance: Longer cast times but bigger payoffs.

Combat and mitigation formulas reworked for steadier, more predictable results.

Spell resists simplified to a flat % system.

AE spells fixed to hit properly even at long range.
[hr][/hr]SimPlayer Updates
CC SimPlayers will interrupt their current cast to cast a CC spell.

Healer SimPlayers will cancel casts if a quick heal is needed.

SimPlayer pullers are more cautious, will bring back potential "adds" safely, and have better target selection.

No more spammy “WTB” messages if they’re already in your group.

Over 100 new SimPlayer dialog lines.

You can now rename SimPlayers in-game with /setname NAME.

SimPlayer population increased to approximately 145 players
[hr][/hr]Spells
Vithean Breeze/Wind/Gale now act as short AE stuns.

Duelist “mana restore” spell line removed.

New Meditate spell for Arcanist and Druid: 8s cast, restores 70% mana (self only).

New Druid Light Healing spell to fill the gap between Minor and regular Healing.

Spell lines (Buff, Haste, etc.) now displayed on item tool tips to clarify stacking.

New droning sound effect while channeling.

Duelist Dooming Undertow slow moved to level 25 (was 34). A new level 34 slow added with a 60% attack speed debuff.

New level 17 Arcanist spell: Ice Shock.
[hr][/hr]Skills
Backstab damage heavily normalized.
[hr][/hr]Items
More resist-focused gear added, trading base stats for higher resistances.

Class vendors for the new class now found in Hidden, Azure, and Loomingwood.

Dozens of new items available to be discovered.
[hr][/hr]System Changes
Added more save-process checks for more reliable Steam Cloud syncs, especially after crashes.

SimPlayer gear loading spread across frames for smoother zone entry.

Spell particle effect scaling options added to reduce visual noise.
[hr][/hr]Zones
New class area added to Port Azure.

Island Tomb fully rebuilt to accommodate larger parties.

Krakengard fully rebuilt to accommodate larger parties.

Bonepits, Underspine, and Fernalla's Revival Plains updated to connect to Willowwatch.

New zone added: Willowwatch.
[hr][/hr]Bug Fixes
Arcanists no longer fail to CC because they stood too far back with wands.

Fixed issue where SimPlayers sometimes stayed idle during combat.

Druid pets less likely to aggro on tanks and ruin pulls.

Sparkle effects no longer incorrectly appear when swapping characters on the select screen.

Many, many more bugs fixed or addressed.







All info is subject to change before 9/26/25. Changes will continue after launch based on community feedback!

notes.title: Erenshor: 2025 Development Roadmap Update
notes.notes:
Hello Erenshor community! 

Erenshor launched almost 2.5 months ago, and from day 1 the community has been providing feedback and ideas for the game's future. I believe I've read just about every single message that has come my way and there have been some pretty consistent themes in there. 

Some recurring themes:

The game plays too fast

The combat is unclear and hard to read

The endgame gets too easy

The middle game gets too hard

We want an Archer / Bard / Summoner / Buff class etc.

WHERE ARE RAIDS??

Using that info, and aligning it with my own vision for the game, I've come up with a development plan for the rest of 2025. 



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43905293/866467dadb46d7064d2b451aeef1bd28c872a1c4.png"]



Increased Party Size: Erenshor players may notice that the game expects certain party roles to be fulfilled: DPS, Heals, Crowd Control, and Tanking. Limiting the party to 4 characters prevents players from expanding on one of these roles to fit their playstyle. You can't bring two healers without sacrificing something else. You can't stack DPS without losing CC or Heals. etc. Adding an extra party slot will allow players to customize their builds more, without punishing themselves.

It goes without saying that this will also require a full game rebalance. 



Smoother Combat Flow: One player put it best to me: Combat in Erenshor just comes down to "Can you out-heal the NPC damage". This stems from:

Mana is 'unlimited' right now with duelist mana restore spells. Mana pool doesn't matter. I plan to address this by removing the duelist mana restoration spell line completely. In-combat mana regeneration will be reduced greatly, and out of combat mana regeneration will be increased greatly. The size of your manapool will matter.

Spell mana costs and SimPlayer spell usage will be tweaked to support this change. An able party should be able to complete encounters without running out of mana through careful mana management.

Healing spells heal for too much right now. You can plan on the max level heal spell 'fully healing' just about any player in the game once you get it. Heal spells will shift to faster cast, lower amounts. You'll be able to decide to top up the tank right now, or wait until he's lower and hit him then. 

Damage is too spiky. Currently, NPCs hit for huge amounts of damage, and can "2-round" a tank in some cases. That's not fun, that's hoping RNG is kind to you. I want to stretch combat out - NPCs will hit for less, but they'll hit at a quicker pace. You'll be able to predict incoming damage and plan your stategy around that. 

NPCs will be getting cast bars so players can plan to interrupt spells. Damage spells longer casting time will help facilitate this. 

MOBs die too fast in many cases (not all cases). With the addition of a 5th party member, their HP pools will need an increase. 



Itemization: Anyone who has played to endgame knows that getting blessed items and ascending them to "purple" is the be-all-end-all of class gearing. Purple items use a formula that adds value to every stat on an item. This ends up making a very select few items BIS for every class. 

In this update, purple items will only enhance stats that already exist on items. So your DPS ring will be better at DPS. Your tanky armor will be better at being tanky. You'll be able to pick and choose which items you want to ascend based on your playstyle. 



Zone Reworks: The dungeons of Erenshor will be expanded in many cases to allow for new named mobs, items, and exploration. Some earlier dungeons (Island Tomb, Krakengard) will need full rebuilds. They're crowded with a party of 4, and 5 will be worse. Expect some renovations. 



During this combat rework this summer, patches will be far less frequent than they've been since launch. This is the first huge content patch Erenshor is receiving, and the game build will not be in a state where I can quickly patch and fix things for the duration of this work. 



The Goal of these reworks is to set the stage for raids: I want to have Erenshor's first raid live by the end of this year. It's really important to me that I start developing raids from a good starting point of game balance. 



I worked for a long time to make all my items purple and now they're being nerfed? TL;DR; Yes, many will be 'less good' than they are now. I understand players have put in a lot of hours to get their characters to build completion and the new purple items may no longer be your BIS. There will be dev commands in game to add Planar Stones and Sivakruxes to your inventory to ascend new items. If you feel that you don't want to do the grind again to get your characters to BIS, I will share those dev commands with you. It's a single player game, we can do things like that :)

notes.title: 5/16/25 - Paladin Update / Sivakrux Update
notes.notes:
Hey all, got some big changes in this one.

IMPORTANT: DODGE AND BLOCK SKILL HAVE CHANGED -- you will need to go to Port Azure to buy your upgraded versions. 

The goal of this patch was to establish Paladin's identities more clearly:

The Tank Paladin: Using sword and shield, Paladins receive mitigation bonuses and rely less on dodge and block. This should lead to more predictable damage rates, having the Paladin be more likely to be 'chipped down' instead of either mitigating everything via Dodge or Block, or taking a big hit. 
The DPS Paladin: Using a 2H Weapon, Paladins forfeit their mitigation bonuses, but gain a 2x attack damage modifier and some new skills. While 2H Paladins may find it harder to tank on-tier content, they'll compliment certain group structures quite well.


Additionally, other classes were dodging and blocking TOO much. By splitting Dodge and Block into different levels, I was able to limit how effective the skills are for non-paladin classes, This will keep Dodge and Block as a "bonus mitigation chance" and not a reliable way to off tank. 

Feedback is welcome (and wanted) on these changes. 

PALADIN CHANGES

 While using a shield, Paladins will gain a 2x bonus to all armor mitigations
 When not using a shield, Paladins will have no armor bonuses
 Damage bonus increased for 2H weapons from 1.3x --> 2x.
Added 2H Skill CLEAVE skill for Paladins. SimPlayers will automatically learn this skill.
  a.) Cleave hits all nearby enemies in front of Paladin.
  b.) Cleave can proc weapon effects
  c.) SimPlayers will not use Cleave if a group member is flagged to CC.
Added 2H Skill Celestial Smite to Paladins. This is a high damage attack.


SKILLS AND ABILITIES

 •Dodge is now broken into SKILL LEVELS (I - IV). Books can be found in Port Azure at the General Book Vendor. Not all classes will be able to use Dodge up to level IV.
 •Block is now broken into SKILL LEVELS (I - IV). Books can be found in Port Azure at the General Book Vendor. Not all classes will be able to use Block up to level IV.


MAPS, PLANARS, SIVAKRUXES


 Sivakruxes will be less likely to drop from any mob (from .1% chance to .01% drop chance)
 Treasure map pieces are far more likely to drop from mobs (from .2%, to 2% drop chance)
 Planar Stones are now extremely rare from mobs (from varied drop chance to .001% drop chance) -- these will be available in raid content.
  -Many players have a large collection of Planar Stones from the previous drop rate
  -Using them will possibly trivialize early raid content - this is your choice as a player: Enjoy the game however you like!
 With the tank changes, higher end content should be easier overall and the feeling of need for "purple" items should be reduced. 


ACHIEVEMENTS

"Is this a Church" and "Climbing is a Bug" are both achievable. Climbing locations will continue to be added. 


BUGS

 Fixed a bug where SimPlayers were not properly proc'ing shields during bash


OTHER

Patch notes now available on the main menu

notes.title: Erenshor: XP Risk v Reward, Bug fixes
notes.notes:
Made some substantial adjustments to how XP rewards are calculated, encouraging players to work through harder content. 


Here's what's going live:

 Fighting higher level mobs than yourself now comes with bonuses. The formula is as follows:
 a.) Enemies all give base XP of (Enemy Level * 4) - this is unchanged and has always been the base value
 b.) Enemies above your level give bonus xp of (Enemy Level * LevelDiff)
     -So a level 15 mob killed by a level 13 player will give (15 * 4) + (15 * 2) xp - then divided by party members
  c.) Bosses and Named mobs will give additional experience (hand set values, please let me know if any are missed)
  d.) Previously, some 'harder' normal mobs had hand added xp modifiers, these are gone in favor of the new system.
  e.) The new system will be overall slightly faster for players adventuring in hard areas, and relatively the same for players battling in easier areas (due to named bonus)
  f.) Rates may continue to be adjusted

 BUG: Can no longer assign more than max ascension points to a rank
 BUG: Found some sounds that didn't respect volume sliders and corrected
 BUG: The achievement for spawning astra is no longer accidentally awarded
 BUG: Can no longer lose inert diamonds by using forge with more than 1 at a time
 BUG: Duskenlight grass will now respect grass quality settings
 TYPO: Planar stones are back to their normal sell value 


Please let me know of any continuing issues!

notes.title: Demo Update: SimPlayer Behavior & More
notes.notes:
Good day all, as development and pre-release preparations continue, it's important that the demo reflects the most up to date state of the game, as such: 


"Pulling" code for SimPlayers has been adjusted quite a bit. They're less likely to 'get stuck' but it still does happen from time to time. This is something that will continue to be addressed. 
The bug where dead SimPlayers refuse to be revived should be totally eradicated (wooo!)
There was an issue with in game fog that could slowly cause visuals to become 'washed out' over time. This is fixed,
GROUP BEHAVIOR:
   -Main Assist (MA): SimPlayers will always target whoever the MA is targeting.
   -If the MA is a player, the SimPlayers will go idle between targets in group combat until the player selects a new target
   -If the MA is a SimPlayer, you can press F2,F3, or F4 (depending on the player's slot) to target that SimPlayer. Press the Fx button again to target that player's target.
   -If the MA dies, the SimPlayers will announce a new, temporary MA in group chat. Upon the MA being revived, the SimPlayers will announce that the original MA is the go-to assist again. 
Navigation Changes: SimPlayers should be less likely to 'get stuck' while following the player. Their new method requires them to sample a valid navmesh from the player's position, or else they'll pause their following until the player is back on valid ground. The performance impact here should be minimal, if any. 
Escape Key Functionality - When pressing escape:
  -If a tutorial window is open, only that will close
  -else if any game windows are open, only those will close
  -else if no windows are open, but the player has an NPC targeted, the target will drop
  -else if none of the above is true, the escape menu will come up

notes.title: Demo Update - February 2nd, 2025
notes.notes:
Happy February all! 

As Erenshor continues on its final stretch of development before Early Access, I feel it's important to continue to make sure the demo is an accurate reflection of what's to come. As such, here are the recent additions:

Game Play: 

Screenshake added on player-casted spells. (can be disabled in options)
New particle effects and SFX for nearly all spells
When turning in quest rewards, you can now drag items to the NPC model to add them to the trade window, instead of having to drag each item to the trade window
Player can now cancel a spell cast by moving during the cast
Font size in the chat log can be scaled from the options menu
SimPlayer Arcanists will be better about refilling player mana
Blessed items on vis gear slots will show a mild particle effect in game on the player or SimPlayer model


Balance / Combat: 

All NPCs do more damage
Players Block and Dodge only trigger if you're facing your attacker
Any non-tank SimPlayer class will try to position itself behind its melee target. Enemies around level 6+ get passive mitigations such as dodge and block. These abilities will only trigger from attacks coming from their front.
SimPlayers are WAY more proficient at using heal spells
SimPlayer tanks will taunt and try to tank all mobs that are not CC'd
SimPlayers will no longer cast DOT spells on full health mobs. This prevents them DOTing a mob that may need to be mezzed if the group choose to engage another target. They'll begin casting DOTs at 95% life.
SimPlayers will no longer 'stack' different crowd control spells on a mob. One is enough, and they know it now.
SimPlayers will be better at 'assisting' whoever is the group tank. If the player is a tank, and the group contains another paladin, the player will be considered 'main tank'. 
SimPlayer pullers will issue an 'attack' command to the group when they return to camp to ensure idle or distant group members engage the target
Pets and charmed mobs will never attack a dazzled target. They'll engage as soon as a player breaks the dazzle.
SimPlayers will not pull if they're out of mana.
SimPlayer target selection and pulling logic is improved
SimPlayers will now pull targets with a spell if possible, instead of "body pulling"
DOTs can now stack between casters, meaning if two druids both cast the same DOT spell on a target, they will both land and do damage. 
Added bonus and penalty to melee damage roles based on the difference between attacker and its target. Red con mobs are harder, blue con mobs are now easier. 
Added a maximum movespeed debuff, maximum attack speed debuff cap on NPCs. Two druids casting snare will have additional effects, however, they do not stack infinitely
Pullers will only target mobs -4 through +5 levels from themselves
SimPlayers will no longer 'spam' status effects on mobs. Once it's on, they won't continuously refresh it


Other: 

Upon exiting the game, a 'backup snapshot' of your game is saved. In the event of data loss due to bad steam cloud syncs or other issues, you can load a local backup from the main menu.
"Reset Simplayer" moved into its own sub-menu on title screen
SimPlayers should be better about choosing equipment to use
Quest turn-ins were sometimes duplicating items, they no longer will
DPS calculation on weapon info cards no longer ignores 'blessed' bonuses
SimPlayers will be less likely to attack trivial mobs while in your group
Combat log is now scrollable
UI performance improvements
Players can no longer cast spells while stunned / dazzled / sleeping, etc
Delay between right clicking and item inspect window showing up is reduced
SimPlayers far below your level will compliment your gear sometimes
Adjusted some word parsing logic to better recognize context
When entering a zone, NPC spawns are 'staggered' over about 4 seconds to prevent trying to perform all of the spawns in one frame (smoother zoning transitions)
Mineral nodes can no longer be mined from infinite distance
Brax's chains no longer gives an attack speed debuff
Dying in a zone would erase all SimPlayer progress gained since entering that zone. This was not intended and is fixed.


Steam Deck: 

Touchpad input will now unlock and show the mouse cursor without first using the DPAD. You may need to select the touchpad-as-mouse profile from your control options.


Please report and be patient with any bugs! Erenshor is an ongoing work in progress and passing new development to the demo always comes with the risk of a new bug. 

Announcements for the Early Access release date are coming soon! Please spread the word about Erenshor, and if you haven't wishlisted the game yet, please consider doing it!

Thank you, as always, for playing Erenshor!
-Brian "Burgee"

New NPCs, Quests, and Mysteries to Solve

There is dark magic present on the island, and a long lost soul whose story must be unraveled once and for all awaits players in this large demo update. Will you decide to help him? Or maybe you'll find other forces at work that earn your trust...

Stowaway's Step's mysteries deepen.

Weather and Lighting
Rain, Clouds, Fog, and Thunder all roll through the skies above the island. Enjoy increased atmosphere from new and improved lighting and visuals including enhanced sunrises and sunsets.

Mining and Crafting
An introduction to Mining and Crafting has been added to the tutorial quest and will bring players a step closer to finding an escape to the Erenshor mainland. 

Re-balanced Combat
The island is a dangerous place, and many enemies have gotten even more dangerous. With a full rework of AC and Stats, combat rewards balanced groups and careful decision making. 

UI Enhancements
A new and improved UI complete with moveable elements to suit Ultra-Wide and other resolutions has been added to the game. A new, more intuitive grouping window will help players discover all of the features that simulated players have to offer.

Meet Dancer! The friendly Duelist Simulated Player has just started out in the tutorial alongside the player. She's always ready to join the group and help the cause. 

Stowaway's Step serves not only as the tutorial to Erenshor, but also as a showcase to many of the features players can expect to find in the main game. The content packed onto the island is meant to give players a preview of everything there is to look forward to. The island is a tiny portion of the main world, and players should expect exponentially more content in the full release.
